claim: The repo reports the Steam ShadowOfWar.exe is wrapped by SteamStub v3.1 (removed with Steamless; .text not encrypted) plus Denuvo Anti-Tamper woven into code, with a near-empty .text and real code in .xtext/.arch sections, image base 0x140000000.
game_build_compatibility: UNKNOWN: repo records no game version, Steam buildid, exe hash or build check; it only states a ~112 MB x64 Steam exe with SteamStub v3.1 + Denuvo (docs/reverse-engineering.md:12,21-29). Our exe is 117732784 bytes (~112.3 MiB), consistent but not proof of 1.0.8874.0 / build 3095001.
verification_method: Static read of repo docs. Verify on our exe by listing PE section names/sizes and checking for a .bind section (read-only header parse; no unpacking needed for this check).
limitations: Steamless unpacking produces a modified copy; whether that is acceptable for our research is a legal/policy decision. Denuvo-mutated functions are opaque to static analysis.
next_experiment: Read-only PE section header dump of our ShadowOfWar.exe; compare to the 17-section list in the repo.
